name.text: Area under a curve above the x-axis

questiontext.text:
The graph shows \(y = {@fx@}\).

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="300px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [{#bxl#}, {#byt#}, {#bxr#}, {#byb#}], axis: true, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); var f = function(x) { return {#cc0#} + ({#cc1#})*x + ({#cc2#})*x*x + ({#cc3#})*x*x*x; }; var lo = {#lo#}, hi = {#hi#}; b.create('functiongraph', [f, lo - 0.5, hi + 0.5], {strokeColor: '#003399', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); var pts = [], n = 60; for (var i = 0; i <= n; i++) { var xi = lo + i * (hi - lo) / n; pts.push([xi, f(xi)]); } pts.push([hi, 0]); pts.push([lo, 0]); b.create('polygon', pts, {fillColor: '#003399', fillOpacity: 0.2, borders: {strokeWidth: 0}, vertices: {visible: false}, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [[lo, 0], [lo, f(lo)]], {strokeColor: '#000000', dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('segment', [[hi, 0], [hi, f(hi)]], {strokeColor: '#000000', dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('text', [lo, {#byb#} * 0.72, 'x = ' + lo], {anchorX: 'middle', fixed: true, highlight: false}); b.create('text', [hi, {#byb#} * 0.72, 'x = ' + hi], {anchorX: 'middle', fixed: true, highlight: false}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Find the exact area of the shaded region between the curve, the \(x\)-axis and the lines \(x = {@lo@}\) and \(x = {@hi@}\).

Area \(=\) [[input:ans1]] square units [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The curve is above the \(x\)-axis from \(x = {@lo@}\) to \(x = {@hi@}\), so the area is the definite integral: the integral adds up thin strips of height \(y\).

\[\text{Area} = \int_{ {@lo@} }^{ {@hi@} } \left({@fx@}\right)dx = \left[{@Fx@}\right]_{ {@lo@} }^{ {@hi@} } = {@Fhi@} - {@Flo@} = {@A@}\]

The area is \({@A@}\) square units.

questiondescription.text:
Integration: area under a curve above the x-axis

Grade 12 CBE Core 4.2: Find the exact area between a positive curve, the x-axis and two vertical lines, by a definite integral.

truefeedback.text: You found \(F({@hi@})\) only; the region starts at \(x = {@lo@}\), so subtract \(F({@lo@})\).
You substituted into the curve's equation, not into its integral. Integrate \({@fx@}\) first.
An area is positive: work out \(F({@hi@}) - F({@lo@})\), upper limit minus lower.
